targets.metric: Survival of daughters orphaned at 5–9.99 y
targets.definition: Hazard of death after the mother's death for daughters orphaned at 5–9.99 y vs daughters whose mother was alive and in the community at the same age, followed from that age.

field.value: females orphaned at 0–4.99 and 5–9.99 y survived less than non-orphans
field.method: survival by age class at maternal loss

accept.basis: direction only: HR > 1 (90% lower bound > 1); insufficient below 300 orphan-years or 10 orphan deaths

targets.notes: Weak: the direction is partly built in by the C8 levers. The 0–4.99 class is reported, not scored (dominated by the self-feeding ramp; see T-DEM-24). Known-age daughters only; transfers followed.

targets.metric: Sex difference in the survival cost of maternal loss at 10–14.99 y
targets.definition: For individuals orphaned at 10–14.99 y: log hazard ratio (orphan vs non-orphan) of sons minus that of daughters.

field.value: males orphaned at 10–14.99 y survived less than non-orphans; females orphaned at 10–14.99 y were no more likely to die than non-orphans and lived longer after the loss than males orphaned at that age; males orphaned at 0–4.99 and 5–9.99 y also survived less
field.method: survival by age class at maternal loss

accept.basis: log HR(sons) − log HR(daughters) at 10–14.99 y > 0 (90% lower bound > 0); insufficient below 200 orphan-years or 10 orphan deaths per sex, or a daughters' HR interval wider than 4-fold

targets.notes: Class-level HRs (sons 0–4.99, 5–9.99, 10–14.99; daughters 10–14.99) reported as unscored parts; sons' post-weaning survival is scored only in T-DEM-15. The asymmetry may also arise from existing sex-specific systems (dominance, male rivalry, female queue).

targets.metric: Stress activation after maternal loss fades
targets.definition: Early-morning stress reading of immatures under 12 orphaned < 2 y before, orphaned >= 2 y before, and non-orphans; mature males orphaned before 12 vs not.

field.value: recently orphaned immatures (< 2 y since loss): diurnal cortisol slope 58% steeper (−0.60 vs −0.38), from higher early-morning cortisol; immatures orphaned earlier did not differ; mature males orphaned before 12 showed no consistent difference
field.n: immatures: 7 recent, 16 earlier, 36 non-orphans (846 samples, 50 individuals; some in more than one class); mature males 11 vs 17 (2,184 samples)
field.method: Bayesian mixed models of diurnal cortisol slope

accept.basis: recent orphans above non-orphans; earlier orphans and adult orphan males not different

targets.notes: Encoded-descriptive: bereaveHalfLifeD and bereaveMaxAgeY were designed from this source; reported, never counted. Truth read of stress at 06:00–08:00 (no diurnal rhythm in the sim).

targets.definition: Lean-mass proxy of individuals aged 4–15 by age and sex: orphans (mother lost after weaning and before 10) vs age-matched non-orphans.

field.value: orphans had less lean mass than age-matched non-orphans (−0.122 ± 0.046 on log SG-corrected creatinine, χ² = 6.376, P = 0.012)

targets.notes: Encoded-descriptive: the feeding lever and condition-to-growth route were designed with this result in view; reported, never counted. The proxy reads the growth record without noise.

targets.metric: Lean-mass proxy: alpha mother vs other mothers
targets.definition: Among 4–10-year-olds with living mothers in the community, lean-mass proxy of the alpha female's offspring vs of other mothers' offspring.

field.value: offspring of subordinate mothers had less lean mass than offspring of the alpha female (−0.292 ± 0.103, P = 0.006); continuous maternal rank not significant (P = 0.093)

accept.basis: offspring of the alpha female higher than of all other mothers; no gradient required

targets.notes: Encoded-descriptive (WP3 finding 1): the feeding deterrence reads dominance relative to the mother, which builds the gradient in; reported, never counted.

targets.metric: Neighbour pressure during pregnancy and offspring survival
targets.definition: Offspring survival (Cox) vs the community's neighbour-pressure index averaged over the 8.5 months before birth, with the source's predictors and controls.

field.value: higher neighbour pressure during pregnancy raised offspring mortality (b = 1.025 ± 0.391, P = 0.008; hazard-ratio 95% CI 1.51–4.85; full model LRT χ² = 9.50, df = 4, P = 0.04); maternal rank no effect (P = 0.55)
field.note: index = mean(I × K) × F, STAR Methods

accept.basis: HR per SD of pregnancy-window pressure > 1 (90% lower bound > 1); insufficient below 30 offspring deaths

targets.notes: The prenatal condition channel (birthCondFromMother) is motivated by this source's hypothesis: a pass is moderate evidence. Touched by any C6/C7a change to encounters, ranging or contact memory made after its value is seen.

targets.metric: Neighbour pressure: pregnancy window stronger than lactation windows
targets.definition: Offspring survival vs neighbour pressure averaged over the first 1, 2 and 3 years of lactation, compared with the pregnancy-window estimate (T-DEM-21 model).

field.value: averaged over the first 1, 2 or 3 years of lactation, neighbour pressure had no effect on survival (P = 0.64–0.80), unlike the pregnancy window (P = 0.008)

accept.basis: pregnancy-window log HR above each lactation-window log HR

targets.notes: Encoded-descriptive: the prenatal channel exists because of this source; reported, never counted.

targets.metric: Aggression received by immatures, by sex
targets.definition: Rate of aggression received (charging displays, chases, attacks) per hour present in the followed party by immatures under 9, by half-year of age and sex.

field.value: aggression received rose faster with age in males (age × sex β = 0.115 ± 0.06, P = 0.04); males received more than females by about 4–5 y (about 3× by 5 y); aggression displayed predicted aggression received (β = 2.694, P < 0.001), not mediated by sex; time in parties with or near adult males did not differ by sex
field.n: 49 immatures under 9 (25 F, 24 M); focal subsample 25 (14 F, 11 M), 2015–2017
field.method: all-occurrence aggression during party follows, per hour observed

accept.basis: age × sex > 0 and male:female rate ratio > 1 at 4.5–6 y (90% lower bounds); insufficient below 10 immatures per sex with >= 20 h at 4.5–6 y

targets.notes: Pre-registered expectation: fail (no juvenile aggression mechanism; supplants skip animals under 5). Reported as a gap, never tuned.

targets.metric: One-year survival after maternal loss, by age at loss
targets.definition: Share of orphans (immatures under 12) alive one year after the mother's death, orphaned under 4 vs at 4 or more.

field.value: one-year survival depended only on age at loss (P = 0.017): 42% of orphans under 4 vs 95% of those 4 or older; at Sonso adopted orphans 100% vs non-adopted 25% (Fisher P = 0.024)

targets.notes: Encoded-descriptive: the self-feeding ramp to each individual's weaning age builds the direction in (adopt() no longer weans at 3); checks the replacement of hazardOrphan; reported, never counted.

protocolLog.param: C8 observer protocols and first computations (freeze commit, before any mechanism): health monitoring (community members seen with respiratory signs, per census day); necropsy truth for found carcasses (disease / aggression, wound complications counted as aggression / other; disappearances unknown) and the last sighting on death records; snare injuries recorded when seen. T-DEM-4: known-cause shares (parts disease, aggression; respiratory share of all deaths reported); T-DEM-5: outbreaks = clusters of sighting days with gaps <= 30 d in which >= 20% of the community is seen ill within 91 d of the first sighting (the registered definition; the 30-d gap is design), per community-year, Poisson interval; T-DEM-6: per outbreak attack = distinct ill / community size, mortality = deaths of members seen ill or with respiratory necropsy from start to 30 d after the last sighting / size, means over outbreaks, part bands attack 0.4-0.9 and mortality 0-0.17 (from the row's basis); T-DEM-7: logistic regression of outbreak death on infant (< 5 y) and >= 30 y, pass if both odds ratios > 1, insufficient below 10 outbreak deaths; T-DEM-8: respiratory deaths (respiratory necropsy, or a disappearance after signs in the previous 30 d) per 1,000 chimp-years; T-DEM-9: share of roster individuals > 3 y alive at each observation-year end whose snare injury was recorded. --demography storage mode (5-min fixes only, no call, event or visit records) for 40-year runs
protocolLog.reason: C8 adds the epidemic and snare mechanisms; protocols written from the rows' definitions before any mechanism code existed

protocolLog.seen: no value exists (sealed, never computed)
protocolLog.param: Implementation choices fixed in the freeze commit before any value, for the sealed rows (src/field/early-life.ts, survival.ts): (1) mixed models approximated: random group intercepts as strata (Cox) or fixed stratum effects (Poisson; strata without events dropped), random individual effects by resampling individuals or mothers in the 1,000-resample cluster bootstrap (seeded, observer-owned); (2) T-DEM-15 first paternity dated at conception (birth - 228 d): crockford2020's reference point is UNVERIFIED in docs/research.md, so the pre-registered default stands; (3) T-DEM-21 I transform: the source text leaves it UNVERIFIED (docs/research.md), so the pre-registered fallback I = max(0, 1 - d/d75) (design) is used; d75 along the ray from the centre (mean of the previous 12 months' fixes) through the encounter; K = (10 - b)/10 for the 10% kernel band b, 0 outside; F = 1 / mean observation days between consecutive encounters in the window (1 / observation days with one encounter; NPI 0 with none); births need 20.5 months of prior observation; (4) T-DEM-14 (outline in §1.12, completed here): 'high-ranking' = top third of the female order at the interval mid-point (jones2010's cut-offs UNVERIFIED; design), intervals after a birth whose infant was alive at the next birth or at censoring, pass if the birth HR (high vs not) 90% lower bound > 1 and the survival-to-1 difference 90% lower bound > 0, survival to 5 a part, insufficient below 30 intervals per group; (5) T-LET-5 (outline completed): expansion month = first month after year 1 in which the winner's 95% range exceeds its year-1 mean by >= 10% (design); pre window 3 y before it, post window 3 y starting one gestation (228 d) later (wood2025 started the post period 8 months after first use of the new area); births and deaths before 3 among them (births without 3 y of follow-up and no death dropped from the share), paired baseline over the same windows; pooled over seeds with an expansion: pass if births rise, the death share falls, and both changes exceed the baseline's; insufficient with fewer than 2 seeds with an expansion; census from the simulation's genealogy (the scenario runs without the observer), kept only in the --unseal run; (6) T-DEM-17's daughters' HR interval width uses the 90% bootstrap interval; (7) T-DEM-23's aggression received = detected decided conflicts lost by the immature
protocolLog.reason: early-life-prereg §1.2 (protocol before mechanism); WP3 findings 8, 22
